title.narrative: Backstage to the Future - A CSO-led Combat against Human Trafficking and Unsafe Migration in Vietnam

description.narrative: This Action is designed with the overall objective of contributing to enhancing the role of CSOs in Vietnams efforts to combat human trafficking, and the specific objective of enabling grassroots CSOs to employ innovative approaches to mobilise and sensitise all levels of society (public, private, civil) to respond to the problem of human trafficking and unsafe migration in 10-15 hot-spot source communities (HSCs) in Vietnam.

description.narrative: OOInd 2 Relevant stakeholders (public, private, civil) have confidence in YU organisational capacity to contribute to the combat against human trafficking.

comment.narrative: According to project baseline research as local Youth Unions have not been actively contributing to the combat against human trafficking the recent times relevant stakeholders have little idea about their organisational capacity to contribute to efforts against human trafficking.

A member of the Standing Committee of a District Party Committee and Vice Chairman of the Peoples Committee of a target District said The number of migrant workers from a target District is the highest in the country with about 15000 people studying and working abroad accounting for 25 of the districts workforce. We believe that cooperation between various agencies is very important especially the roles of the Youth Union the Womens Union local government and businesses in the area. As district leaders we assess that the capacity of the Youth Union staff has improved showing growth in management skills and project reception. They are ready to take on development project opportunities for the district.

description.narrative: OOInd 1 Number of Youth Unions (YUs) as CSOs plan and deliver actions that directly tackle issues of human trafficking in the five target localities.

comment.narrative: According to the project design between 59 YUs in the five localities of Qung Ninh H Long City Hi Phng Hi Phng City and Thy Nguyn District Ngh An Ng An City and Din Chu District Qung Bnh ng Hi City and B Trch District and H Tnh Nghi Xun District and Can Lc District will plan and deliver actions that directly tackle issues of human trafficking in the five target localities.

By the third year of the project 20232024 YUs in Hi Phng Sn District and Ng Quyn District in Hi Phng City and Thy Nguyn District Qung Bnh B Trch District and ng Hi City and H Tnh Can Lc District and Nghi Xun District developed 6 action plans which were incorporated into 4 contracts each with a budget plan and an activity plan which were delivered in all these 7 locations.

title.narrative: OPInd 2.1 A bespoke training curriculum to build capacity for YUs to engage private sector in antihuman trafficking actions.

description.narrative: OPInd 2.1 A bespoke training curriculum to build capacity for YUs to engage private sector in antihuman trafficking actions.

comment.narrative: Following the Forum Theatre training in the first year the project organised in the third and final year more training and planning and mentoring workshops in creative communication stakeholder engagement and action planning and management. Each training or workshop was provided with pre and postsurvey where participants were asked to evaluate their level of knowledge and skills in the training subject. Each training or workshop also developed bespoke training materials that respond to the need of the participants which was collected during the presurvey. In 2024 during project final evaluation members of the YUs were asked again to rate their level of level of skills and knowledge gained not only from participating in the project training and workshop programme but also from leading the project implementation themselves. All indicators show significant increase. Participants also offered positive reflections on the level of skills and knowledge that have gained from taking part in the project.

comment.narrative: Output 3 has been revised to reflect the implementation of the project. During the third and final implementation year where most ontheground activities were taking place it has been learned that there was little interaction between local Youth Unions and the private sector. This situation was explained by two main reasons i those identified as private sector with relevance to the project was labour export businesses and there was not many of these ii labour export businesses and other local businesses who participated in project activities kept their level of engagement at awareness level. In this situation local Youth Unions diverted their stakeholder engagement plans to include those who could be more involved and their involvement could yield more meaningful impact. These relevant stakeholders included local High Schools for engagement with students aged 1518 Womens Unions for engagement with young men and women and local television and radio services for engagement with the wider population. The engagement of these local stakeholders was effective in getting useful knowledge and information about safe migration across the main atrisk audience resulting in higher local awareness of human trafficking risk and safe behavioural change. Along with detailed guidance from the project we discussed with related departments worked with Kaizen a labour export company to plan the activities. When we did it we understood many things and came up with many initiatives. Like creative communication activities forum theatre. Instead of hiring a professional drama team for all schools we assigned the schools to develop the script and perform by themselves. This makes us work harder but it improved the capacity of YU staff at the schools and the content would be closer to each locality which would attract more attention from the audience. In short it was hard work but we found it really practical and meaningful when we ourselves could decide how to do it how to implement it. A YU leader and project participantMy memorable moment was successfully organising a televised panel discussion on Migration Past and Future in collaboration with the provincial broadcasting station. Despite challenges the flagship program attracted 20000 viewers overcoming obstacles through interagency cooperation. A YU member and project participantBefore I thought that trafficking only happened to gullible people with less education and mainly women in mountainous areas but when participating in the project activities I understood that victims and criminals of trafficking can be anyone and unsafe migration will have high risks of turning me into victim of trafficking. This really made me completely change my mind about the plan of studying abroad and finding overseas jobs that my parents had arranged for me. Because my parents had been abroad for many years they trusted their acquaintances and friends in taking me there. But as I know from the project anyone can be a broker or a trafficker regardless of whether they are relatives or friends. It wouldnt hurt if I am more prudent in this matter. A High School student

comment.narrative: During the first year of the project members of 9 YUs in Qung Ninh H Long City Hi Phng Hi Phng City and Thy Nguyn District Ngh An Ng An City and Din Chu District Qung Bnh ng Hi City and B Trch District and H Tnh Nghi Xun District and Can Lc District received training in Forum Theatre which equipped them with new skills and knowledge in devising theatre work as a tool for communication in preventing human trafficking. They continued to cascade the skills and knowledge to the wider network of YU members and young people in their locality. Deputy Secretary of a target District Youth Union noted The most notable impact of the project is that it has helped teachers learn how to create scripts and coordinate stage forums. For students who are members of the Youth Union in schools besides playing characters they also get to be the audience and participate in debates to find solutions for situations. As for myself I have gained more knowledge about the topic of human trafficking prevention and creative communication has helped my daily work attract more interest from Youth Union members in the district. Secretary of the Youth Union in a target District reflected The project equipped me with skills in idea generation planning teamwork and communication strategies.
